transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Maya Santos (Redwood AE), Alex Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Triton), Jonah Reyes (Triton), Lina Ortiz (Triton), Marco Velas (Triton)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be fuzzy):
- Discovery call to understand Triton's model selection needs: open models vs managed, context window, multilingual support, tool-calling for internal search and live ad-catalog lookups.
- Customer leaning toward private/VPC for ad-content PII and residency but wants cost SLOs; interested in Dedicated POC for throughput tests.
- Security questions: SOC 2, KMS, audit logs, data retention and SSO.

Topics: model comparisons, context length, multilingual, function/tool calling, hosting options (hosted/dedicated/private), security/compliance, POC next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we have about 50 minutes so we'll try to cover the model fit and the tooling pieces, and then next steps for a POC if that sounds right.
[00:23] Priya: yeah thanks Maya, quick context — Triton Mediaworks runs personalized video ad generation and a large Q&A knowledge base for brand partners, so two main workloads: prompt-heavy generation with long context (scripts and multi-turn prompts) and high QPS retrieval+rerank for ad-serving.
[00:40] Maya: awesome, and can you share what you're using now?
[00:45] Jonah: sure, today it's a mix — some in-house LLMs on prem for sensitive assets and some OpenAI for experiments, plus a home-grown retrieval service. We're also evaluating Mistral, llama-3 style forks and Falcon 40B open models for cheaper cost.
[01:05] Alex: okay, so main decision levers will be latency/cost, context window, and tool-calling compatibility. do you have an expected latency SLO for ad-serving?
[01:18] Priya: for the ad-serve rerank path we want <80ms 95p ideally, but we know that's tight; for generation batch jobs we can tolerate a few seconds.
[01:30] Lina: and from security, any hosted option needs to satisfy SOC two and SAML SSO, HSM/KMS support, and audit logs. data residency is also a concern — some partner data has residency clauses.
[01:45] Maya: totally understood. quick note on wording — SOC 2 (some transcribers show sock two) is standard, we support SOC2 and ISO in our security pack. We also offer a Private deployment for full VPC/on-prem scenarios plus Dedicated capacity for reserved GPU pools.
[02:02] Marco: can you unpack differences between Dedicated and Private?
[02:10] Alex: yeah so Dedicated is Redwood-managed reserved GPU capacity in our cloud with isolation and predictable throughput; it still uses our control plane but dedicated instances and SLAs. Private is customer-controlled control plane (VPC or on-prem) for stricter compliance — you can use your own KMS/HSM, full network controls. there is a tradeoff in ops overhead and sometimes cost.
[02:36] Priya: what's the implication for model selection — like if we pick an open model such as Mistral or RedPajama is that straightforward on Private?
[02:46] Alex: generally yes, we onboard open models routinely — runtime supports various quantization paths, and for Private we can bring the same model artifacts. the main differences are kernel/compilation tuning and sometimes sequence-length optimizations; for very long context windows we may choose a different memory layout or swap to bigger GPU types.
[03:10] Jonah: long context is a key ask — we routinely feed 32k tokens of transcript+metadata in the generation flow, with some cases pushing to 64k. what's the realistic path?
[03:22] Alex: okay that explains a lot. Redwood runtime supports variable context lengths; however, model selection matters — some open models have native 8k or 16k token training and we can fine-tune or use context stitching. for 32k/64k you often need models pre-trained for long context or apply windowing + KV cache tricks. there is a cost/latency impact since larger windows increase memory and token-serve cost.
[03:48] Priya: can you give a ballpark on cost delta? like hosted per-token vs dedicated per-token?
[03:55] Maya: rough numbers in the benchmark matrix we'll send — hosted is usage-based so higher per-token but less ops. Dedicated amortizes GPUs across throughput so lower per-token at scale, but requires commit and we add reserved pricing. we'll include examples for 8k vs 32k contexts.
[04:15] Marco: tool-calling — we need function calls into our ad-catalog and a live pricing microservice. does Redwood handle tool calling and streaming function responses?
[04:27] Alex: yes, we support function/tool calling, streaming responses and structured output; for Private we add network policies so function calls route to your internal services. sometimes function calling requires schema pinning and versioning — we recommend a test harness.
[04:45] Lina: any caveats on PII leaving the VPC?
[04:49] Maya: Private keeps data in your VPC and you can configure no-telemetry policies. with Dedicated (Redwood-managed) you can opt-in to contracts that limit data retention and keep logs encrypted; for truly sensitive PII we recommend Private or on-prem.
[05:05] Jonah: curious about quantization and latency on cheaper models — you mentioned runtime picks kernels; does Redwood do that dynamically?
[05:13] Alex: yeah the runtime selects kernels and quant paths based on model architecture and sequence distribution. we also do continuous batching and KV caching to reduce per-token latency/cost. sometimes for 4-bit quantization you get a bigger latency benefit but risk small quality diffs — we surface quant-recommendations in Redwood Optimize.
[05:33] Priya: how often do you see hallucinations with the quantized open models?
[05:38] Alex: varies by model and workload; part of our evaluation is running your prompt set to measure hallucination rate and answer consistency. we'll include those metrics in the bench.
[05:50] Marco: competition question — we've talked to Anthropic and Bedrock teams; how do you compare on observability?
[05:58] Maya: our Console exposes token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. we try to be more ops-focused for engineering teams.
[06:10] Priya: timeline — internal stakeholders: infra, legal, and product. we'd like a POC within 2–3 weeks and a pilot with dedicated capacity in 6–8 weeks depending on legal. is that realistic?
[06:25] Maya: yes that's typical, we can run a 2-hr Dedicated throughput slot in the first week and have a signed statement of work to start Dedicated pilot within 6–8 weeks pending contracts.
[06:36] Lina: for contracts we need KMS/HSM integration details and an SLA for uptime and latency; also audit log retention options.
[06:46] Maya: we'll send the security whitepaper and your legal can sign an NDA if needed. our Private offering supports customer-managed KMS and we capture audit logs per request.
[06:58] Jonah: about multilingual — our ad inventory spans EN/ES/PT/FR and some APAC languages, so we need a model with decent multilingual quality or a tiered approach. any recommended open models?
[07:10] Alex: Mistral and some Llama-3 forks have strong english coverage, for multilingual you might consider models fine-tuned or open models like Mistral xline or dedicated multilingual forks. we can run evaluation across your test set and also suggest translation+post-edit flows if needed.
[07:30] Priya: for ad generation we care about brand tone — can you do evals for style adherence?
[07:35] Alex: yes we run style/regression tests tied to prompt sets and can set threshold alerts for quality drift.
[07:42] Marco: any blockers for running an initial bench on our sample prompt set? we can share 100 prompts and some load profile.
[07:49] Maya: perfect. action: Priya will share prompt set and SLOs, Alex will propose POC config.
[08:00] Priya: quick note on data retention — we like 30 day logs for debugging but need ability to purge specific partner data. is that supported?
[08:10] Maya: yes — retention policies are configurable in Dedicated and Private; hosted API can offer retention terms via contracts.
[08:18] Jonah: SLA details — what's a typical latency SLA for Dedicated?
[08:22] Alex: we publish per-model latency profiles and Dedicated comes with latency targets based on committed throughput; exact numbers depend on model size and GPU choice, we'll include examples.
[08:34] Priya: technical deep dive possibility — after this we'd like a session focused on 32k+ context architecture and memory tuning. can Alex lead?
[08:43] Alex: happy to — suggest a 60–90 minute technical deep dive with infra and model devs.
[08:50] Marco: good. also curious about cost modeling for bursty traffic — ad serving spikes a lot. how do you handle burst capacity?
[08:58] Maya: Dedicated has burst/buffer options and autoscaling policies; we can reserve a baseline and allow bursts with overprovisioning or fallback model variants to keep latency within SLOs.
[09:12] Lina: for legal we need an exported artifact describing where logs live and encryption-at-rest details.
[09:18] Maya: we'll attach the security whitepaper and a KMS integration note.
[09:24] Priya: i have a question about tool calling rate limits and concurrency — our microservices have strict rate limits. can Redwood rate-limit or queue function calls?
[09:34] Alex: yes you can set per-route rate limits and retries. for high QPS we often recommend a local sidecar or gateway to smooth bursts and avoid hammering internal services.
[09:46] Marco: any weird gotchas with long-running KV caches and memory pressure?
[09:52] Alex: with large KV caches and 64k contexts memory becomes the limiter; we can shard context, use external KV stores or configure eviction policies. we'll propose a few architectures in the POC doc.
[10:05] Priya: how do you manage model rollouts and fallbacks? for example if a quantized variant regresses we want automatic fallback to float variant.
[10:16] Alex: rollouts are supported — canary, A/B, automatic fallback to a compatible variant. Redwood Console surfaces regressions and allows pinning and rollback.
[10:27] Maya: ok quick pause — we've covered a lot, i want to confirm next steps.
[10:32] Maya: action items recap: Maya to send benchmark matrix and security docs; Alex to propose POC config; Triton to share prompt set and SLOs. we'll set up a 2-hour slot for Dedicated throughput testing.
[10:45] Priya: sounds good. can you also include cost scenarios for 8k vs 32k vs 64k context?
[10:52] Maya: yes will include tiered cost models.
[11:00] Marco: one last ops question — observability hooks: can we get trace IDs per request to join with our existing tracing stack?
[11:08] Alex: yes, we can attach trace IDs and provide tracing hooks; Console integrates with common APMs.
[11:15] Lina: ok thanks, that helps.
[11:20] Maya: great, unless anyone else has burning Qs we'll wrap and propose times for the technical deep dive and Dedicated slot.
[11:27] Priya: no further Qs, thanks.
[11:30] Jonah: thanks all.
